Biopsy of the healing tissue shows abundant macrophages with an anti-inflammatory phenotype that is promoting repair of damage caused by the worm and by eosinophil and mast cell degranulation. Which of the following cytokine pairs most likely drove this macrophage phenotype?

explanation.summary: IL-4 and IL-13 promote activation of macrophages to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, which repairs helminth-related tissue damage.
explanation.whyCorrect: IL-13 and IL-4 promote the activation of macrophages to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype (alternative macrophage activation with enhanced fibrosis/tissue repair). M2 macrophages are critical in the repair of tissue damage due to tissue-invasive helminths and eosinophil and mast cell degranulation.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IFN-gamma from Th1 cells activates macrophages to a microbicidal phenotype that kills phagocytosed pathogens, not an anti-inflammatory repair phenotype.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-12 and IL-1 are pro-inflammatory cytokines secreted by activated macrophages in Th1 responses.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-17 and the chemokine IL-8 promote neutrophil infiltration and inflammation, the opposite of the M2 repair response.
whyWrongByChoice.E: IL-5 activates eosinophils and IL-2 is a T cell growth factor; neither drives M2 macrophage activation.

questions.stem: In an in vitro experiment, IL-17 is added to cultures of fibroblasts, endothelial cells, and epithelial cells. The culture supernatant is then found to attract neutrophils. Which of the following products induced by IL-17 in these non-immune cells most directly explains the neutrophil attraction?

explanation.summary: IL-17 induces chemokines such as IL-8 from many cell types, ultimately promoting neutrophil infiltration and activation.
explanation.whyCorrect: IL-17 induces the production of many other cytokines (IL-6, IL-1beta, TGF-beta, TNF-alpha), chemokines (IL-8), and prostaglandins from many cell types including fibroblasts, endothelial cells, epithelial cells, and macrophages. Ultimately IL-17 primarily promotes neutrophil infiltration and activation, and it can also enhance monocyte recruitment and stimulate defensin production.

whyWrongByChoice.A: IFN-gamma is produced mainly by Th1 cells to activate macrophages; it is not the chemokine responsible for neutrophil attraction.
whyWrongByChoice.B: IL-13 promotes mucus, peristalsis, and M2 macrophages in helminth responses and does not recruit neutrophils.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IL-4 is a Th2 cytokine that drives IgE class switching; it is not an IL-17-induced neutrophil chemoattractant.
whyWrongByChoice.D: IL-5 activates eosinophils and is secreted by Th2 cells, not induced from fibroblasts by IL-17.

questions.stem: A researcher compares antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity against a helminth with ADCC against an antibody-coated tumor cell. Which of the following antibody-receptor combinations triggers eosinophil degranulation onto the surface of the worm?

choices.label: E
choices.text: IgG bound to MHC class I

explanation.summary: Eosinophils kill helminths when bound IgE on FcepsilonR1 recognizes its cognate antigen; NK cells use IgG and CD16 against abnormal cells.
explanation.whyCorrect: IgE binds the high-affinity IgE receptor FcepsilonR1 on eosinophils and mast cells. When helminth antigens cross-link FcepsilonR1 through IgE, eosinophils degranulate, releasing toxic granule proteins such as major basic protein that directly kill the worm. This is the eosinophil form of ADCC, distinct from NK cells recognizing IgG through CD16.

whyWrongByChoice.A: CD40 is the receptor for CD40L on helper T cells and does not bind IgE.
whyWrongByChoice.C: IgG recognized by CD16 (FcgammaRIIIA) is the NK cell ADCC mechanism against infected or malignant cells, not eosinophil killing of helminths.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Fas is a death receptor bound by FasL on CTLs; it does not bind antibody.
whyWrongByChoice.E: MHC class I presents peptide to CTLs and inhibits NK cells; it is not an Fc receptor.
